variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Variables are immutable. You use 'let' to bind them. Shadowing is commonly used to 'update' a variable's value in a scope.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Gleam is statically typed with inference. It compiles to Erlang or JavaScript. Custom types are equivalent to ADTs or enums.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
let add_int = 5 + 3
let add_float = 5.0 +. 3.0

let div_int = 5 / 2
let div_float = 5.0 /. 2.0
let rem_int = 5 % 2

let logic = True && False || True

let eq = 5 == 5
let neq = 5 != 3
operators.notes: Gleam distinguishes between Int and Float operators (e.g., '+' vs '+.'). Equality '==' works for all types.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Gleam does not have an 'if' statement. Instead, it relies completely on exhaustive 'case' pattern matching for all conditionals.

for_loop.title: For Loop (Mapping)
for_loop.notes: Gleam has no loops. Standard library functions like list.map, list.filter, and list.fold handle iterative operations.

while_loop.title: While Loop (Recursion)
while_loop.notes: Statefulness and iterative loops are handled entirely through tail-recursive function calls.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions are defined with 'fn'. The pipeline operator '|>' is widely used to pass results as the first argument of the next function.

arrays.title: Lists and Tuples
arrays.notes: Lists use `[..]` for fast cons/prepend operations. Tuples are accessed via index e.g., `.0`, `.1`.

maps.title: Maps (Dicts)
maps.notes: Dictionaries (dict) provide immutable key-value stores. Since everything is immutable, inserting returns a new dict.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Gleam uses the Result type exclusively for errors. The 'use' keyword provides an elegant syntactic sugar for handling early returns on errors.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
% Line comment in Erlang
-doc("Function doc").
add(A, B) -> A + B.
comments.notes: Gleam uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Gleam supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
IsActive = true,
Result = IsActive andalso not false.
booleans.notes: Gleam treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Gleam performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Gleam represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Gleam formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
case Response of
    {ok, Data} -> Data;
    {error, _} -> error
end.
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Gleam, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Gleam constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: Gleam achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: Gleam emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Gleam are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Gleam uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Gleam provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: Gleam isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
